title: Current Electricity
syllabus: Electric current, Flow of electric charges in a metallic conductor, Drift velocity, Mobility and their relation with electric current; Ohm's law, Electrical resistance, V-I characteristics (linear and non-linear), Electrical energy and power, Electrical resistivity and conductivity; Temperature dependence of resistance; Internal resistance of a cell, Potential difference and emf of a cell, Combination of cells in series and in parallel, Kirchhoff's laws and simple applications, Wheatstone bridge, Metre bridge.

questions.question: The resistance of a wire is $R\,\Omega$. If it is melted and stretched to $n$ times its original length, its new resistance will be: (NEET 2017)
questions.solution:
Volume remains constant: $V = A L = A' L' \implies A' = \frac{A L}{n L} = \frac{A}{n}$.
$$R' = \rho \frac{L'}{A'} = \rho \frac{n L}{A / n} = n^2 \left(\rho \frac{L}{A}\right) = n^2 R$$

questions.question: A set of $n$ equal resistors, each of value $R$, when connected in series give an equivalent resistance of $X$. If these $n$ resistors are connected in parallel, the equivalent resistance will be: (NEET 2018)
questions.solution:
In series: $R_s = n R = X \implies R = \frac{X}{n}$.
In parallel: $R_p = \frac{R}{n} = \frac{X/n}{n} = \frac{X}{n^2}$.

questions.question: In a metre bridge, the balance point is found to be at $39.5\text{ cm}$ from the end $A$, when the resistor $Y$ is of $12.5\,\Omega$. The value of resistor $X$ in the left gap is: (NEET 2021)
questions.solution:
From the balance condition of a metre bridge: $\frac{X}{Y} = \frac{l}{100 - l}$.
$$\frac{X}{12.5} = \frac{39.5}{100 - 39.5} = \frac{39.5}{60.5} \implies X = 12.5 \times \frac{39.5}{60.5} \approx 8.16\,\Omega$$

questions.question: A cylindrical conductor of length $L$ and uniform area of cross-section $A$ has resistance $R$. Another conductor of length $2.5L$ and resistance $0.5R$ of the same material has area of cross-section: (NEET 2020)
questions.solution:
$R = \rho \frac{L}{A}$.
For the second conductor: $R' = \rho \frac{L'}{A'} \implies 0.5R = \rho \frac{2.5L}{A'}$.
$$A' = \frac{\rho (2.5L)}{0.5R} = \frac{2.5}{0.5}\left(\rho \frac{L}{R}\right) = 5A$$

questions.question: The drift velocity of free electrons in a conducting wire carrying a current $I$ is $v_d$. If both the current and the radius of the wire are doubled, the new drift velocity will be: (NEET 2022)
questions.solution:
Current $I = n e A v_d = n e (\pi r^2) v_d \implies v_d = \frac{I}{n e \pi r^2} \propto \frac{I}{r^2}$.
$$v_d' = \frac{2I}{(2r)^2} v_d = \frac{2}{4} v_d = \frac{v_d}{2}$$

questions.question: A battery of emf $E$ and internal resistance $r$ is connected across a variable external resistor $R$. The maximum power dissipated in the resistor $R$ is: (NEET 2016)
questions.solution:
By the Maximum Power Transfer Theorem, power delivered to the external load is maximum when $R = r$.
$$P_{\text{max}} = I^2 R = \left(\frac{E}{R + r}\right)^2 R = \left(\frac{E}{2r}\right)^2 r = \frac{E^2}{4r}$$

questions.question: The temperature coefficient of resistance of a wire is $0.00125^\circ\text{C}^{-1}$. At $300\text{ K}$, its resistance is $1\,\Omega$. At what temperature will its resistance become $2\,\Omega$? (NEET 2019)
questions.solution:
$T_0 = 300\text{ K} = 27^\circ\text{C}$ where $R_0 = 1\,\Omega$.
$$R_t = R_0[1 + \alpha(t - 27)] \implies 2 = 1[1 + 0.00125(t - 27)]$$
$$0.00125(t - 27) = 1 \implies t - 27 = \frac{1}{0.00125} = 800 \implies t = 827^\circ\text{C}$$
$$T = 827 + 273 = 1100\text{ K} \text{ (or } 1127\text{ K when referenced directly from } 0^\circ\text{C})$$
Referenced from $0^\circ\text{C}$: $R_{27} = R_0(1 + 27\alpha) = 1$, $R_t = R_0(1 + \alpha t) = 2 \implies \frac{1 + \alpha t}{1 + 27\alpha} = 2 \implies 1 + \alpha t = 2 + 54\alpha \implies \alpha t = 1 + 54(0.00125) = 1.0675 \implies t = \frac{1.0675}{0.00125} = 854^\circ\text{C} = 1127\text{ K}$.

questions.question: Two cells having the same emf $E$ but different internal resistances $r_1$ and $r_2$ are connected in series with an external resistance $R$. If the potential difference across the terminals of the first cell becomes zero, then $R$ is equal to: (NEET 2021)
questions.solution:
Circuit current $I = \frac{2E}{R + r_1 + r_2}$.
Terminal voltage of 1st cell $V_1 = E - I r_1 = 0 \implies E = I r_1$.
$$E = \left(\frac{2E}{R + r_1 + r_2}\right)r_1 \implies R + r_1 + r_2 = 2r_1 \implies R = r_1 - r_2$$

questions.question: Kirchhoff's first law (Junction rule, $\sum I = 0$) and second law (Loop rule, $\sum \Delta V = 0$) are based respectively on the conservation of: (NEET 2020)
questions.solution: Kirchhoff's Junction rule expresses conservation of electric charge, while the Loop rule expresses conservation of electrostatic energy in a closed circuit loop.

questions.question: Mobility of free electrons is defined as the drift velocity per unit electric field ($\mu = v_d / E$). Its SI unit is:
questions.solution: $$\text{Unit of } \mu = \frac{\text{m/s}}{\text{V/m}} = \frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}} \times \frac{\text{m}}{\text{V}} = \text{m}^2\cdot\text{V}^{-1}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$$

questions.question: A carbon resistor is marked with rings of colors in sequence: Brown, Black, Red, and Gold. The resistance value is:
questions.solution:
Color code values: Brown $= 1$, Black $= 0$, Red $= 10^2$, Gold $= \pm 5\%$.
$$R = 10 \times 10^2\,\Omega \pm 5\% = 1000\,\Omega \pm 5\% = (1.0 \pm 0.05)\,\text{k}\Omega$$

questions.question: In a balanced Wheatstone bridge, the resistances in the four arms are $P = 10\,\Omega, Q = 20\,\Omega, R = 30\,\Omega,$ and $S = 60\,\Omega$. If the positions of the galvanometer and cell are interchanged, the balance condition:
options: Remains unchanged and no current flows through the galvanometer
Doubles the current through all resistors
questions.solution: By the conjugate arms property of a Wheatstone bridge, interchanging the battery and galvanometer branches leaves the bridge in exact balance.

questions.question: Two electric bulbs rated $220\text{ V}, 40\text{ W}$ and $220\text{ V}, 60\text{ W}$ are connected in series across a $220\text{ V}$ mains supply. Which bulb will glow brighter?
options: Both will glow with equal brightness
questions.solution:
Resistance $R = \frac{V^2}{P} \implies R_{40} > R_{60}$.
In series, current $I$ is identical through both bulbs.
Power dissipated $P = I^2 R \propto R$. Since $R_{40} > R_{60}$, the $40\text{ W}$ bulb dissipates more power and glows brighter.

questions.question: Three identical cells each of emf $E$ and internal resistance $r$ are connected in parallel. The effective emf and internal resistance of the combination are:
questions.solution: For $n$ identical cells connected in parallel, equivalent emf remains $E_{\text{eq}} = E$, and equivalent internal resistance is $r_{\text{eq}} = \frac{r}{n} = \frac{r}{3}$.

questions.question: When a current of $2\text{ A}$ flows through a cell for $10\text{ s}$, its terminal voltage is $4\text{ V}$. If the emf of the cell is $6\text{ V}$, the internal resistance of the cell is:
questions.solution:
During discharging: $V = E - I r$.
$$4 = 6 - (2)r \implies 2r = 2 \implies r = 1.0\,\Omega$$

questions.question: As temperature increases, the electrical resistivity of a metallic conductor and a semiconductor respectively:
questions.solution: In metals, rising temperature increases thermal lattice vibrations, decreasing relaxation time $\tau$ and increasing resistivity ($\rho \propto 1/\tau$). In semiconductors, charge carrier density $n$ increases exponentially with temperature, decreasing resistivity ($\rho \propto 1/n$).

questions.question: A wire of resistance $12\,\Omega$ is bent in the form of a complete circle. The effective resistance between two diametrically opposite points is:
questions.solution:
The circular ring splits into two equal semicircular branches, each having resistance $R_1 = R_2 = \frac{12}{2} = 6\,\Omega$ connected in parallel.
$$R_{\text{eq}} = \frac{6 \times 6}{6 + 6} = 3\,\Omega$$

questions.question: If $n, e, A,$ and $v_d$ represent number density of free electrons, electronic charge, cross-sectional area, and drift velocity respectively, the current density $J$ is given by:
questions.solution: $$J = \frac{I}{A} = \frac{n e A v_d}{A} = n e v_d$$

questions.question: In a metre bridge experiment, null point is obtained at $20\text{ cm}$ from one end when a resistance of $10\,\Omega$ is in the left gap and an unknown resistance $R$ is in the right gap. The value of $R$ is:

A current of $5\text{ A}$ passes through a copper wire of cross-sectional area $1\text{ mm}^2$. If the number density of free electrons is $8.5 \times 10^{28}\text{ m}^{-3}$, the drift speed of electrons is approximately:
questions.solution: $$v_d = \frac{I}{n e A} = \frac{5}{(8.5 \times 10^{28}) \times (1.6 \times 10^{-19}) \times (10^{-6})} = \frac{5}{1.36 \times 10^4} \approx 3.68 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m/s} = 0.37\text{ mm/s}$$

questions.question: An electric heater is designed to operate on $220\text{ V}$ with a power of $1100\text{ W}$. The current drawn and the resistance of the heating coil are:
Twelve equal resistors, each of resistance $R$, are connected to form a skeleton cube. The equivalent resistance between two diagonally opposite corners of the cube is:
questions.solution: By symmetry and current distribution: $V = I\left(\frac{R}{3}\right) + I\left(\frac{R}{6}\right) + I\left(\frac{R}{3}\right) = I R\left(\frac{2}{6} + \frac{1}{6} + \frac{2}{6}\right) = \frac{5}{6} I R \implies R_{\text{eq}} = \frac{5}{6}R$.

questions.question: The equivalent resistance between points $A$ and $B$ for a balanced Wheatstone bridge having $5\,\Omega$ resistors in all five branches (four arms and the central galvanometer branch) is:
questions.solution:
Because the bridge is balanced ($5/5 = 5/5$), no current flows through the central branch. The circuit simplifies to two parallel branches of $(5 + 5) = 10\,\Omega$ each:
$$R_{\text{eq}} = \frac{10 \times 10}{10 + 10} = 5\,\Omega$$

questions.question: Under what condition is the terminal potential difference across a cell greater than its electromotive force ($V > E$)?
options: When the cell is being charged by an external source
When the cell is discharging through an external resistance
When the cell is in an open circuit
questions.solution: When a cell is charged, current is driven into its positive terminal from an external charging source: $V = E + I r > E$.

questions.question: Relaxation time $\tau$ of free electrons in a metallic conductor is related to electrical conductivity $\sigma$ by:
questions.solution:
Drift velocity $v_d = \frac{e E \tau}{m}$.
Current density $J = n e v_d = \left(\frac{n e^2 \tau}{m}\right)E = \sigma E \implies \sigma = \frac{n e^2 \tau}{m}$.

questions.question: Two electric bulbs rated $25\text{ W}, 220\text{ V}$ and $100\text{ W}, 220\text{ V}$ are connected in parallel to a $220\text{ V}$ supply line. The total power consumed by the combination is:
questions.solution:
In parallel across the rated voltage, powers add directly:
$$P_{\text{total}} = P_1 + P_2 = 25\text{ W} + 100\text{ W} = 125\text{ W}$$

questions.question: A cell of emf $E$ and internal resistance $r$ is connected to an external resistance $R$. The graph of terminal potential difference $V$ versus current $I$ drawn from the cell is:
options: A straight line with negative slope $-r$ and intercept $E$
A straight line with positive slope $+r$
A parabola passing through the origin
A horizontal straight line parallel to the current axis
questions.solution: The relation is $V = E - I r = (-r)I + E$. This represents a linear equation $y = mx + c$ with negative slope $m = -r$ and vertical intercept $c = E$.

questions.question: Constantan and Manganin alloys are widely used to make standard resistance coils because they possess:
options: High resistivity and nearly negligible temperature coefficient of resistance
Low resistivity and high temperature coefficient
Low melting point and high ductility
questions.solution: Standard resistors require values that remain stable despite operating temperature fluctuations. Manganin and constantan provide high electrical resistivity coupled with an exceptionally small temperature coefficient of resistance $\alpha$.

questions.question: A piece of copper and a piece of germanium are cooled from room temperature ($300\text{ K}$) to liquid nitrogen temperature ($77\text{ K}$). Their resistances:
options: Decreases for copper and increases for germanium
Increases for copper and decreases for germanium
questions.solution: Copper is a metallic conductor (positive $\alpha$), so cooling reduces lattice vibrations and decreases its resistance. Germanium is a semiconductor (negative $\alpha$), so cooling decreases free carrier concentration and increases its resistance.

questions.question: A wire of resistance $R$ is cut into 5 equal parts and these parts are connected in parallel. The equivalent resistance of the parallel combination is $R'$. The ratio $R / R'$ is:
questions.solution:
Resistance of each part is $r = R/5$.
When 5 such parts are placed in parallel: $R' = \frac{r}{5} = \frac{R/5}{5} = \frac{R}{25}$.
$$\frac{R}{R'} = 25$$

questions.question: The V-I characteristic curve of a non-ohmic device (such as a semiconductor p-n junction diode) is:
options: Non-linear and does not obey Ohm's law
A straight line passing through the origin
A straight line parallel to voltage axis
Independent of the sign of applied voltage
questions.solution: Non-ohmic conductors exhibit non-linear $V\text{-}I$ characteristics where the ratio $V/I$ is not constant and dynamic resistance varies with current and voltage polarity.

questions.question: $N$ identical cells each of emf $E$ and internal resistance $r$ are connected in series with an external resistance $R$. If the polarity of one cell is reversed by mistake, the effective emf and internal resistance of the combination are:
questions.solution: Reversing one cell opposes another cell, reducing total active aiding cells to $(N - 2)$, so $E_{\text{net}} = (N - 2)E$. However, internal resistance is non-directional and all cells remain in series: $r_{\text{net}} = N r$.

questions.question: The resistance of a $100\text{ W}, 200\text{ V}$ lamp is:
A fuse wire should have:
options: High resistivity and low melting point
Low resistivity and high melting point
High resistivity and high melting point
Low resistivity and low melting point
questions.solution: A fuse wire requires high resistivity to generate sufficient Joule heating ($H = I^2 R t$) during an overcurrent surge and a low melting point so it melts rapidly to break the circuit.

questions.question: In a metre bridge with resistances $P$ and $Q$ in the gaps, balance point is at $l_1 = 40\text{ cm}$. When a resistance of $10\,\Omega$ is connected in series with $P$, the balance point shifts to $60\text{ cm}$. The original value of $P$ is:
questions.solution:
Case 1: $\frac{P}{Q} = \frac{40}{60} = \frac{2}{3} \implies Q = 1.5P$.
Case 2: $\frac{P + 10}{Q} = \frac{60}{40} = \frac{3}{2}$.
$$\frac{P + 10}{1.5P} = \frac{3}{2} \implies 2(P + 10) = 4.5P \implies 2P + 20 = 4.5P \implies 2.5P = 20 \implies P = 8\,\Omega$$

questions.question: Three unequal resistors $R_1, R_2,$ and $R_3$ are connected in parallel across a battery. Which physical quantity is the SAME for all three resistors?
questions.solution: Components connected in parallel share common junction nodes at both terminals, maintaining the exact same potential difference across each component.

questions.question: A total charge $Q$ flows through a resistor according to $q(t) = 2t^2 + 3t + 5\text{ (in C)}$. The electric current at $t = 2\text{ s}$ is:
Two copper wires of lengths $l$ and $2l$ have radii $r$ and $2r$ respectively. The ratio of their specific resistances (resistivities) is:
questions.solution: Specific resistance (resistivity $\rho$) is an intensive property of the material and does not depend on the dimensions (length or radius) of the conductor.

questions.question: A uniform wire of resistance $20\,\Omega$ is cut into two equal halves. These two halves are then joined in parallel. The equivalent resistance is:
questions.solution:
Each half has resistance $R_1 = R_2 = 10\,\Omega$.
$$R_{\text{eq}} = \frac{10 \times 10}{10 + 10} = 5\,\Omega$$

questions.question: An ideal voltmeter and an ideal ammeter have internal resistances equal to:
questions.solution: An ideal voltmeter draws zero current from the branch it measures ($R_v = \infty$). An ideal ammeter introduces zero series resistance drop ($R_a = 0$).

questions.question: A battery of emf $10\text{ V}$ and internal resistance $3\,\Omega$ is connected to a resistor. If the current in the circuit is $0.5\text{ A}$, the terminal voltage of the battery is:
A current of $1.6\text{ mA}$ flows through a conductor. The number of electrons crossing any cross-section per second is:
questions.solution: $$I = n e \implies n = \frac{I}{e} = \frac{1.6 \times 10^{-3}\text{ A}}{1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}} = 1.0 \times 10^{16}\text{ electrons/s}$$

questions.question: In a mixed grouping of $m$ rows, each containing $n$ identical cells of emf $E$ and internal resistance $r$, the current through external resistance $R$ is maximum when:
questions.solution: Total internal resistance of the bank is $r_{\text{eq}} = \frac{n r}{m}$. By the maximum power transfer condition, current delivered to external resistance $R$ is maximum when $R = r_{\text{eq}} = \frac{n r}{m}$.

questions.question: Ohm's law is valid when the physical state of the conductor (such as temperature, strain) remains constant because:
options: Ratio of electric field to current density remains constant
Number density of electrons changes linearly
questions.solution: Ohm's law in microscopic vector form is $\vec{J} = \sigma \vec{E}$. When temperature and strain are constant, conductivity $\sigma = \frac{n e^2 \tau}{m}$ is constant, making current directly proportional to potential difference.

questions.question: A wire of resistance $4\,\Omega$ is stretched uniformly to twice its original length. The percentage increase in its resistance is:
